method: Root reviewed all selected sentences, with neighbouring source context for ambiguous selections. Post-result diagnostic review, not independent blind gold, complete source labels, or a record-eligibility decision.

categories.guidance_related: Forecast, reaffirmation, withdrawal, qualification, or relevant comparison wording. Includes repetitions, fragments and unresolved scope; not one completed fact per sentence.
categories.context_or_past_not_a_current_forecast: Past/current performance, old guidance, analyst wording, source context or present operations. May support a quote or baseline, but cannot alone be accepted as a current management forecast.
categories.ambiguous_outlook_or_operating_intention: Vague opportunity, intention or potentially relevant outlook whose eligibility needs independent source-level adjudication. Not automatically a false positive.

rows.text: Robust revenue growth in retirement, ASO, and PO highlights the durability of our model and reinforces our expectations of a long secular growth runway for these businesses.

Our ASO and PO worksite employee growth continues to outpace the industry, reflecting our value in navigating regulatory complexity and ensuring compliance often for clients with no or, as I said, limited HR support.
Our PO business remains strong with high single-digit worksite employee growth driven by robust demand and record retention rates.
January enrollment in our at-risk Florida MPP medical plan went well and in line with our expectations, helping drive sequential revenue growth.
We remain on track to exceed our fiscal 26 synergy targets we discussed last quarter.
Leading indicators such as bookings and broker referrals have re-accelerated to pre-acquisition levels, and we are adding sales headcount to capture the demand we see.
We are gaining momentum cross-selling paychecks ASO, PO, and retirement solutions to PayCore's clients, and we continue to win larger than expected ASO deals and broker-referred PEO opportunities.
Following successful pilots last quarter, we are scaling the use of our voice and email agents for payroll processing, enabling service teams to focus on proactive, higher value advisory support.
We also expanded our agentic AI sales and service tools to the entire sales team with a goal to drive revenue growth and efficiency.
Excluding a pay core, we estimate that expenses grew in the low single digits during the quarter.
Shifting to our guidance for FY26, which is based on current market conditions, we reaffirm our prior fiscal 26 outlook, except for raising our interest on funds held for client expectations.
Interest on funds held for clients is now expected to be in the range of $200 to $210 million.
All other guidance metrics remain unchanged.
We would anticipate fourth quarter growth to be approximately 12%, with an adjusted operating margin of 41% to 42%.
However, our second half outlook remains consistent with our expectations in the organic revenue growth acceleration we saw in Q3.
But if you go back to Q4 of last year, I think we've seen sequential improvement each quarter in the organic growth of the business.
So if you look at the first half, total revenue organic growth was roughly 4%, and that improved from Q1 to Q2.
And then when you look at the back half, whether it's Q3 or Q4 combined, we would expect it accelerated in Q3, and we would expect to see similar organic growth.
growth performance in Q4.

findings: The .25 screen selected 104/673 sentences. It retained all 12 positive-labelled parent passages, but only 21/22 frozen positive sentence controls: parent retention hides the S483 exclusion miss.

S483 scores .0629 despite whole-source context. S486-S488 retain its parent QA016 for different outlook wording. Keeping a parent does not establish that the specific exclusion was identified or attached.
At .5, controls S199 (.3634), S483 (.0629) and S652 (.2960) are filtered; at .25 only S483. Some controls are qualifications or repetitions, not distinct facts.

All eight frozen negative controls are below both cutoffs, but other selected statements describe actual performance: for example S044 (.7635), S358 (.5255), S644 (.5759). Eight correct controls do not establish overall precision.
S322/S512/S513 are analyst context, not independent management forecasts. Correct use still requires management confirmation and a fact-role judgment.
Native sentences include fragments (S134 and S364), so sentence detection alone is not a complete quote or fact boundary.
Compared with the same-call passage screen, direct sentence targeting costs 729.94s vs 200.33s, 60073 vs 17800 input tokens, and two vs one native sequences. Full end-to-end savings are unmeasured.

Do not lower the cutoff to the observed S483 score or add a fourth repair layer. The alternative has a measurable parent-coverage/cost tradeoff, but is not a certified safe sentence filter or complete extraction solution.
